Historically the allies took the path, fell on the Burgundian flank, and finished it within the hour. (5 turns / 43 counters)

・Okehazama, 1560 - The Imagawa have 33 counters to the Oda's 16, but can move only five a turn; the Oda move everything, every turn. And Oda Nobunaga has a way to win that has nothing to do with the score: destroy the Imagawa Yoshimoto counter, and the battle is over at once. Can he close the road behind Yoshimoto before Yoshimoto withdraws? (9 turns / 49 counters)

・Sekigahara, 1600 - The battle the game is named for. The 28,000 Mori troops on Mount Nangu stay where they are only for as long as they are held in check. The Kobayakawa on Mount Matsuo change sides from noon. How far can the Eastern Army push before the defection, and how much can it spare to watch Mount Nangu? Can the Western Army hold its crane's-wing line to the end? (8 turns / 72 counters)

・Waterloo, 1815 - What Napoleon lacked was not men, but the number of orders he could issue at once. The French have 36 counters but can move only 12 at a time, with four places to take at once: Hougoumont, La Haye Sainte, the ridge itself, and Plancenoit at their back. Wellington, for his part, must not only yield nothing on the ridge but also come out ahead in the attrition. (11 turns / 78 counters)

・Gettysburg, 1863 - Three days of battle. The Union holds the fishhook ridge and the short interior line; Lee must work around the long outer line and keep attacking, because standing still does not move the score. Should Howard have gone north of the town? Why did Lee strike the centre again on the third day? (20 turns / 107 counters)

・Chancellorsville, 1863 - The largest field in the game, with each counter roughly a regiment. The battle opens an hour before Jackson's flank attack. The Union has one task - do not give up the crossroads - but can move only 40 of its 227 counters each turn. The Confederates must take the crossroads in the west while a thin line of trenches holds Fredericksburg, ten miles to the east. (10 turns / 374 counters)

Many more battlefields are included.

Deep, but playable in 30 minutes: most battles are decided within 15 to 45 minutes. Only Chancellorsville runs to about two hours.

The free demo includes six battlefields: Nancy, Bowang, Okehazama, Sekigahara, Gettysburg and Waterloo.

■ Open the opponent up

The AI here is not a single block. "Use the river as a defensive line." "Avoid encirclement." "Read what the enemy is trying to do." Forty-eight separate routines stack up into one commander's judgement.

You can switch them off one at a time, from a list inside the game. Build a general who never uses rivers, or one who never reads your intent, and watch what changes. Whatever makes this AI difficult, you can take apart and examine.

There are nine temperaments: standard, defensive, offensive, delaying, manoeuvre, ultra-cautious and seizing - plus relentless assault, and plain incompetence.

■ Build your own battlefields

A full scenario editor is included. Lay the hex grid, paint the terrain, run the rivers and the roads, place the counters, set the victory conditions. Every battlefield in the game opens in the same editor, so you can begin by changing the deployment at Sekigahara - and then set the general of your choice against a map of your own.

■ Features

・Mandatory combat - any unit in an enemy Zone of Control must attack

・Combat groups resolve as one-against-many or many-against-one - never a shapeless melee

・Artillery with range and line of sight

・Terrain that decides battles: river crossings, fortifications, ridges, woods, marsh

・Seven-level graded victory, with separate conditions for each side

・Opposing generals with distinct temperaments - from relentless assault to plain incompetence

・Held-back reserves, surprise attacks, sudden-death objectives, reinforcement schedules, defection

・A full scenario editor - modify the included battlefields or build your own

・Interactive tutorial and an in-game rulebook

・Eight languages: English, Japanese, Spanish, French, German, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese and Korean

■ An advisor, if you want one

Hex-and-counter games are not hard because the rules are complicated. They are hard because nothing tells you which of forty legal moves is the one that matters. Ask the advisor and it will show you what it would do and why - or hand it a phase and let it play. Turn it off when you no longer need it.

FORGE YOUR PATH, A UNIQUE STORY EVERY RUN

Enter a vast fantasy world shaped by war, ambition, and shifting alliances. In Sellsword, you are not a chosen hero, but a mercenary forging your own path.

Choose your character, develop your build, and decide how you survive, fight, and earn your place in a world at war. Everything you do is recorded in your journal. Death can come often, but every life leaves behind a unique story.

A KINGDOM AT WAR

Explore an interconnected world divided between rival kingdoms and factions. Take contracts from lords, settlements, and powerful groups as you travel through dangerous territories.

Fight bandits, creatures, and enemy forces. Explore ruins, caves, and contested lands in search of wealth and opportunity.

PROCEDURAL QUESTS & MAIN STORY

Choose who to serve and complete different quests on every run. Your actions, choices, and encounters shape the story of your current character.

Follow the main story or create your own path through a world where no two lives unfold the same way.

KEY FEATURES

  • Choose from different characters with unique playstyles

  • Build your character around melee, ranged, or hybrid combat

  • Explore a large interconnected world

  • Take contracts from factions, lords, and settlements

  • Fight bandits, creatures, and organized forces

  • Navigate shifting alliances and rival factions

  • Build your reputation through your actions

  • Enjoy sandbox freedom combined with quest-driven progression

  • Create a unique story with every run

Send Forth the Brave is a solo-developed roguelike deckbuilder where you manage an Adventurers’ Guild.

Instead of fighting battles yourself, you organize adventuring parties by combining cards in your hand — weapons, items, soldiers, and heroes — then send them on commissions to earn gold and reputation.

Every commission requires careful planning. Prepare your team, meet the client’s requirements, and decide how to best use your limited resources. Ordinary soldiers and items can be reassigned freely, while unique heroes will only return after completing their missions.

Build your guild, attract powerful adventurers, discover legendary equipment and relics, and take on increasingly challenging commissions.

Complete commissions to earn gold and positive reviews:

Fulfill your clients’ strange and varied requests to earn gold and positive reviews. Different client types behave differently—some start leaving negative reviews from the very first turn, some reduce their rewards over time, and others may even try to poach your best team members… Carefully handle their tricks, deploy your cards wisely, assemble the right teams, and claim every coin and every positive review.

Choose the path you believe in:

Strength, Agility, or Wisdom? Each path grants different bonuses and attracts different heroes to your guild. Progress along your chosen path, raise your rank, earn respect, and unlock legendary heroes, weapons, and items!

Spend gold to expand your roster:

Hire new personnel and purchase new items and weapons from a variety of shops to build a powerful, well-rounded adventuring team capable of satisfying increasingly demanding clients!

Plan your schedule and build the finest Adventurers’ Guild:

Manage your days wisely! Opening for business is a solid choice, but there is much more to do: take part in random events, accept gifts, visit wondrous shops to expand your roster, and perhaps even encounter mysterious clients who may offer relics imbued with great power… A wide variety of events and paths await.

Demons Want Earth. Bad Idea.

Satan wants Earth. Unfortunately for him, you're ridiculously overpowered, the demons just keep coming, and you have a frankly unreasonable amount of firepower at your disposal.

Send Them to Hell is a chaotic 2.5D action roguelite where you slaughter massive demon hordes, build increasingly ridiculous combinations of upgrades, and see just how far you can push your power before everything on screen explodes.

Play solo or bring up to 3 friends along for the slaughter. Fight your way through hellish battlefields, discover powerful items, cast ultimate abilities, and turn yourself into a walking apocalypse.

Kill Demons. Break Your Build. Beat Your Friends' Scores. Repeat.

Fight Your Way Through Multiple Game Modes

Your mission in Adventure Mode is simple: survive five expanding biomes, grow stronger with every run, and take the fight straight to Satan himself.

But why stop there?

  • Adventure Mode - Battle through five biomes in a campaign that culminates in a showdown with Satan.

  • Endless - The hordes don't stop coming. How long can your build keep you alive?

  • Weekly Challenge - Take on a fresh challenge and compete for the highest score on the leaderboards.

  • The Fractured Earth - Descend through a floor-based dungeon where every run offers another chance to fight deeper and push further.

Bring Friends. Cause Problems.

Demons are a lot less intimidating when four heavily armed lunatics are mowing them down together.

Team up with up to 3 friends in online co-op and turn the battlefield into an absolute disaster for Satan's army. Work together, stack your upgrades, and see what happens when everyone's builds start getting out of hand.

Of course, you can always compete for the high score afterward. Friendship is temporary. Leaderboards are forever.

Build Something Absurdly Powerful

Every run is another chance to discover a devastating combination of upgrades. With over 100+ items, unlockable Legendary Items, powerful Tomes, and a full Perk Tree, there are plenty of ways to turn an ordinary demon hunter into an extinction-level crusader.

Experiment with different upgrades. Unlock new abilities. Find combinations that make the hordes regret showing up.

And when a run ends? Take what you've earned, improve your character, and jump back into the slaughter even stronger than before.

Earth Isn't Going to Defend Itself

Satan made the first move. Now it's your turn. Send Them (back) to Hell.

Disclaimer:

Demons were definitely hurt in the making of this game.

"Wait for me, sweetheart. Grandma's on her way."

The whole world has been swallowed up by hordes of hideous monsters. How scared and lonely you must be, holding down the fort all by yourself... I'm sorry, dear. Grandma's late. Even if the sky comes crashing down, Grandma will find you. Just stay alive for me. Grandma will put her life on the line to hold you in her arms again!

"Everyone here? Old soldiers never die!"

The world may have gone mad and rotten monsters may be running rampant, but who dares lay a finger on our grandkids! Just picturing our little darlings trembling alone at home sets us grandmas' and grandpas' hearts on fire. Even if our grandkids have gone all the way to Mars, we'll chase after them to the very end!

Alright then. It's time for us grandmas and grandpas to dig out the good old "conversation starters" we used back in the day.

How Grandma and Grandpa Fight

Allow us to show off our prized possessions: the gear from our glory days, worn smooth by our own hands.

Grandma's Scooter Power

My joints are bad, so I need something to get around!

Choose your weapon and abilities!

Max out Grandma and Grandpa's physical stats!

Equipment Delivery

Take the dropped equipment and find Grandma's best friend, Delivery Cart Grandma!

So what are you waiting for? Join us already!

Become a club member and come rescue our grandkids with us!
